figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Hierarchical Clustering of 82 Newly Identified and 17 Previously Known Representative Tetracycline Biosynthetic Gene Clusters. The
names of strains harboring representative TC BGCs, also referred to as representative strains, are shown. Numbers in parentheses following each
representative strain indicate the total number of gene clusters predicted to produce the same or structurally similar compounds. Seventeen
representative strains with known products are highlighted in blue, with the corresponding TC natural products listed in parentheses. In contrast,
82 newly identified representative BGCs are predicted to encode TC natural products with novel structures. Notably, three groups of novel
compoundsmisiomycins, varsomycins, and hibarimicins J−Lwere identified from strains highlighted in red. The right panel shows the
abundance of selected protein types encoded by these BGCs, with circle size proportional to the number of corresponding proteins.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Discovery and Proposed Biosynthetic Pathway of Misiomycins. (A) The mis gene cluster responsible for the biosynthesis of misiomycins
from Streptomyces misionensis DSM 40306. (B) HPLC analysis of metabolites from wild-type DSM 40306 and mutant strains. (C) Proposed
biosynthetic pathway for misiomycins A−D.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Discovery and Proposed Biosynthetic Pathway of Varsomycins. (A) The var gene cluster responsible for the biosynthesis of varsomycins
from Streptomyces varsoviensis NRRL ISP-5346. (B) LC−MS analysis of metabolites from wild-type NRRL ISP-5346 and mutant strains. (C)
Proposed biosynthetic pathway for varsomycins A and B. The ORTEP diagram for the crystal structure of 8 is shown, with CCDC deposition
number 2308212.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Discovery and proposed biosynthetic pathway of hibarimicins. (A) The hib cluster responsible for the biosynthesis of hibarimicins J−L
from Saccharothrix australiensis DSM 43800. The hib cluster is split into two regions by the aus cluster, which encodes a hybrid type I PKS/NRPS.
(B) HPLC analysis of metabolites from wild-type DSM 43800 and mutant strains. (C) Proposed biosynthetic pathway for hibarimicins J−L. The
ORTEP diagram for the crystal structure of 24 is shown, with CCDC deposition number 2308236.
